(By Sri.KRS., Adv.,)
 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.35,00,000/- with costs and interest from date of accident till date of realization, in respect of death of Priyanka.V.C., who succumbed to injuries on 12.08.2023 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 12.08.2023 at about 10.35 a.m., the petitioner No.1 and his deceased wife were proceeding towards Siddalingeshwara Temple, Yadiyur as rider and pillion rider in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EQ- 7313.
At that time one tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-TB- 0628 and trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-6702 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident, the pillion rider i.e., wife of the petitioner No.1 fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body and succumbed to injuries on the spot.
3. Immediately after the accident deceased was shifted to CHC Kunigal, wherein the duty doctors examined the deceased and declared dead on the way to the hospital wherein post mortem was conducted.

The petitioners have incurred huge amount towards transportation of body, funeral,
hospitalization and other expenses.

4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was very hale and healthy and was aged about 23 years and she was working as Gare coolie and she was earning Rs.600 to 800/- per day from said avocation and she used to contribute all her earnings towards maintenance of her family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony and their lives have came to stand still.

The petitioner No.1 is the husband and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the daughter and son of the deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have became miserable and hence this petition.
5. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with interest.
6. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
notices were issued against respondents.

Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before Naveen Kumar Y M vs Raju K C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66221092/
2 this court.

sentences.text: Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 is placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has filed written statement on its behalf and denying the entire petition averments.
The insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
They also denied the expenses made towards funeral and other ceremonies.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
He also denied the other contents of the petition.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.
On 18.03.2025 leaned counsel for the respondent No.2 has submitted that there is no respondent evidence on behalf of respondents.
Hence, prayed to post the case for the arguments.
Prayer was taken on record.

As per the prayer of learned counsel for respondent No.2, the respondent evidence was taken as closed and the case was posted for arguments.
8.
I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Priyanka.V.C. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.08.2023 at about 10.35 a.m., near Sri.Siddalingeshwara Swamy Temple Check Post, Yadeyuru, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur due to the rash and negligence driving of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-TB- 0628 by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative.
 Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders for  the following:-
 REASONS  ISSUE NO.1:

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 12.08.2023 at about 10.35 a.m., the petitioner No.1 and his deceased wife were proceeding towards Siddalingeshwara Temple, Yadiyur as rider and pillion rider in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EQ- 7313.
At that time one tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-TB- 0628 and trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-6702 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said vehicle.
Due to the impact of accident, the pillion rider i.e., wife of the petitioner No.1 fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body and succumbed to injuries on the spot.
12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.

Ex.P.1 FIR and complaint which reveals that one Naveen Kumar.Y.M. has lodged complaint on 12.08.2023 against the driver of the respondent offender vehicle tractor bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-TB-0628 and trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-6702.
Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The Ex.P.3 is the Inquest report which clearly discloses that, deceased has died on 12.08.2023 in a Road Traffic Accident.
Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar along with sketch which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV report.

Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet which reveals that, police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offender vehicle tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-TB-0628 and trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-6702.
13.
The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondents.
During the course of cross-examination of petitioner nothing was elicited from the mouth of petitioner, so as to disbelieve his version.

14. Learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has addressed detail arguments on behalf of the respondent and has filed memo with 2 citations stating that no interest shall be awarded against future prospects and the sum for loss of love and affection being 50,000/- and for consortium of Rs.40,000/- could not have been granted to each of 3 dependents separately, therefore prayed to accept the contentions raise by the respondent in this case.

However, it is apparent on the face of records that the respondents have admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-TB-0628 and trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-6702.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.

The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-TB-0628 and trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-6702.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
15.
The PW.1 in his evidence has deposed that, his deceased wife was working as Gare Coolie and was earning Rs.600 to 800/- per day.
His wife was aged about 23 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioners being husband, daughter and son of the deceased

,
were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, she being a sole bread earning member Naveen Kumar Y M vs Raju K C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66221092/
4 in her family.

sentences.text: He has further deposed that, he has spent huge expenses towards funeral and other expenses.
16. Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No. 2 and 3 are the daughter and son of the deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of himself, petitioner No.2 and deceased and birth certificate of petitioner No.3.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased.
Since, the respondents have not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
17.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
(i) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 23 years.
As per the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.7, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 02.02.2000, the accident was occurred on 12.08.2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 23 years.
(ii). Income of the deceased: According to the petitioners deceased was working as Gare coolie and earning a sum of Rs.600/- to 800/- per day.
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

18. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

entities.text: Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
19.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.16,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year 2023 and thus income of the deceased is to be considered at Rs.16,000/- per month.
20. Loss of dependency:
The following points are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.

5 (ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

sentences.text:
21. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased is aged below years and therefore 40% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is determined as Rs.6,400/- (16,000 X 40/100 = Rs.6,400/-).

Therefore the total income of the deceased is determined as Rs.22,400/- per month (16,000 + 6,400 = Rs.22,400/-).
22.
Admittedly, petitioner No.1 to 3 are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, when there are 2 to 3 Dependents 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As such 1/3rd amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e.,
Rs.22,400/-.
When the said 1/3rd amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.14,934/- (Rs.22,400 - Rs.7,466 = Rs.14,934/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, total loss of income from the deceased comes to (Rs.14,934/- X 12 X 18 =Rs.32,25,744/-).
Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.32,25,744/-.

23. Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:- In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But they have not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sethi and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 24. Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e.,
(15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Further, for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/-
i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).

sentences.text: Like wise for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Similarly, for loss of love and affection to the extent of Rs.25,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).
Loss of consortium:
it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40,000/-).
(ii) Towards parental consortium:

Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the daughter and son of the deceased and have lost love and affection of the mother and hence, they are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under this head (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40000/-).
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

Accordingly,
I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
26.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.34,34,744/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 40:30:30.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1, 70% shall be released to petitioner No.1 on his proper identification and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
The entire amount awarded to the petitioners No.2 and 3, shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, till they attain the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
